transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—thanks for coming today. What brings you in to see me?

I came in because... well, I just can't stop feeling like everything that goes wrong is my fault. Like, I’m a terrible employee, and a bad homeowner, and I just deserve to lose everything I’ve worked for. It's funny because when I bought the house, the realtor—he was this guy named Gary, wore these incredibly loud ties—he said, "Oh, you're going to love the neighborhood." And I did, for a while. There was this stray cat that used to come around, an orange tabby. I named him Marmalade. I used to buy the expensive wet food for him, but then he just stopped showing up one day. I always wondered if someone else took him in or if... well, you know. But anyway, yeah, I just feel like I'm failing at everything right now and it's all my fault.
How long have you been feeling this way—that everything is your fault and you're failing at things?

Well, the depression and just... not caring about anything anymore, that's been going on for about two years and one month. I remember exactly because it started right around the time my sister had her baby shower. It was at this little Italian place downtown, the one with the red and white checkered tablecloths? They had this amazing garlic bread, just dripping in butter, but I couldn't even bring myself to eat any. My sister was wearing this beautiful yellow dress, and everyone was so happy, and I just sat there feeling like a ghost. I ended up leaving early and telling her I had a migraine, which wasn't true, but I just couldn't stand being around all that joy when I felt so... empty. I haven't really been back to that restaurant since, which is a shame because their eggplant parmesan is supposed to be incredible. But yeah, about two years and a month now of just feeling this way.
Over these past two years, has your mood been low and empty pretty much every day without a break, or have there been weeks or months here and there where you felt back to your normal self?

Looking back... yeah, it's pretty much been there the whole time. The low mood, just not caring about anything. I mean, there were maybe a couple of brief periods where I could function a little better, like... oh, last spring, I managed to plant some marigolds in the front yard. I bought them at this little nursery out on Route 9. The owner there is this sweet older lady, she always gives me a discount because I used to go to school with her nephew. He was a drummer in the marching band, actually. Really good, too. They went to state my junior year. We had to ride this awful yellow school bus for six hours to get to the competition, and the AC was broken the whole time. It was a nightmare. But anyway, yeah... the emptiness has been there almost the entire time since it started, just kind of hanging over me, except for those tiny little breaks where I could maybe water a plant or something.
During this two-year period, have you also noticed significant changes in your sleep, appetite, or energy, or trouble concentrating, alongside the low mood?

Yeah, my sleep has been... really bad, actually. Most nights I just lie awake for hours, just listening to the house settle. You know how old houses make those weird creaking noises? It always sounds like footsteps on the stairs, but it's just the wood expanding or something. I actually had a guy come out to look at the foundation last year because I was convinced the whole place was sinking. He was this really tall guy, wore these thick glasses, and he told me it was fine, just normal settling. He charged me like two hundred dollars just to tell me that, which felt like a rip-off, but what are you going to do? I tried to dispute the charge with my credit card company, but they said since he provided a service, they couldn't do anything. I use that card for everything to get the miles, you know? I was hoping to take a trip to Seattle eventually. I've always wanted to see the Space Needle. But yeah, anyway, after I finally fall asleep, I usually wake up around three or four in the morning, and then I just can't get back to sleep before work. It's exhausting.

Before this two-year period began, had you ever experienced an earlier episode of depression that lasted at least a couple of weeks and then fully resolved, with you feeling completely back to your normal self afterward?

I don't... I don't really think so. Before the baby shower, I was doing okay. At least, I don't remember feeling this bad for that long before. I mean, I had bad days, sure. Like when I first started my job as an operations specialist, I was so stressed out. They threw me right into this massive software migration project on my second week. We were moving from this old legacy system to a cloud-based one, and nobody knew what they were doing. The IT guy, Kevin, he was always eating these really loud, crunchy potato chips right next to my desk while we were trying to figure out the data mapping. It drove me crazy. I actually bought noise-canceling headphones just because of him. They were the really expensive ones, too, the kind they use on airplanes. I got them in silver, though I kind of wished I got black because the silver got scuffed up in my bag. I used to carry this huge leather tote bag that weighed a ton... but no, to answer your question, I don't think I ever had a time where I felt depressed like this for weeks and then it just went away. This is really the first time it's been this bad.
During this two-year period, have you ever had thoughts of death, of not wanting to be alive, or of harming yourself?

I haven't really had thoughts of hurting myself, no. I mean, I just feel empty, like I said. But not like I want to die. Though, honestly, sometimes when I'm driving to work, I get so zoned out on the highway. I take I-95, and the traffic is just horrendous in the mornings. There's this one merge lane near exit 14 that is basically a death trap because people refuse to zipper merge. I don't understand why it's so hard for people to just take turns. It's like they think letting one car in front of them is going to delay their whole day. I actually saw a bumper sticker the other day on this rusty green Honda Civic that said, "I brake for hallucinations," which I thought was kind of funny, but also weirdly specific. The guy driving it was wearing a backwards baseball cap and vaping... it smelled like artificial strawberry, even with my windows rolled up. I hate that smell. It reminds me of this lip gloss I used to wear in middle school. But no, I don't want to hurt myself or anything like that. I just want to feel normal again.
Over these past two years, have you noticed any significant changes in your appetite or weight—either eating much more or much less than usual, or losing or gaining weight without trying?

My appetite has been... well, it's really been all over the place. Mostly I just end up skipping real meals during the day. I'll just live on coffee and toast, or whatever is easiest to grab. Like, I have this toaster that my mom got me for Christmas a few years ago. It's one of those retro-looking ones, bright cherry red. It matches absolutely nothing in my kitchen because my kitchen has all stainless steel appliances and these really ugly oak cabinets that the landlord refuses to paint. I asked him if I could just paint them white myself, and he said no because it would "ruin the natural wood grain." But it's not even nice wood! It looks like it belongs in a cabin from the 1980s. Anyway, I was putting some bread in the toaster the other day—just plain sourdough, I get it from this bakery down the street that always smells like cinnamon—and I realized that my jeans were feeling really loose. Like, I had to pull my belt to the tightest notch. So I guess I've been losing weight without really trying, just because I don't have the energy to cook anything more complicated than toast.

During this two-year period, has there been a stretch of at least two weeks where your mood and energy were so low that it seriously affected your ability to function at work or in daily tasks, compared to how you're doing generally?

Yeah, I guess there have been times like that. Like, I'm still working, but it takes so much effort just to keep up with the basics. I've been making mistakes, too. Enough that my supervisor actually pulled me aside to check in on my performance. Her name is Brenda, and she has this really intense way of looking at you over the top of her reading glasses. They're these thick tortoiseshell frames, and she always wears them on a chain around her neck. The chain has these little fake pearls on it. It jingles when she walks down the hallway, so you always know when she's coming. I actually tried wearing glasses chains for a while because I thought it was a practical idea—I'm always losing my sunglasses in my car. But it just felt like it was getting tangled in my hair all the time. My hair is getting pretty long now, I haven't had a haircut since... I don't even know. I just haven't had the energy to make an appointment. 

But yeah, it's not just work. I've missed social plans, and the townhouse is just... it's a disaster. It's way messier than I can usually stand. There's laundry piled up on this armchair I have in the corner of my bedroom. It's a really nice armchair, actually, I got it at a vintage market downtown. It's this deep mustard yellow velvet, which sounds ugly, but it's actually really cool. Or it was, before it just became a giant laundry hamper. I bought this special upholstery cleaner for it, but I haven't even taken it out of the box. So, yeah, it's been really hard to just function normally.

Yeah, my sleep has been pretty awful lately. Most nights I just lie awake for hours, just listening to the house settle. It makes these weird creaking noises, especially the floorboards in the hallway. The wood in this place is so old. I think I mentioned my landlord before, the one with the ugly oak cabinets? Well, he also refuses to fix this one floorboard right outside the bathroom that squeaks every time you step on it. I tried putting a rug over it—this really nice woven runner I found at Target, it has these geometric patterns in navy and cream—but it doesn't help muffle the sound at all. I actually bought a second rug, a thicker one, but I haven't put it down yet because it's still rolled up in the plastic in the corner of my living room. I keep meaning to unroll it, but the plastic is sealed with that really tough packing tape that you can never find the end of. You know what I mean? You just end up scratching at the roll for ten minutes. 

Anyway, I'll finally fall asleep, but then I wake up around three or four in the morning, and I just can't get back to sleep before work. I just lie there, staring at the ceiling fan. It has this one blade that's slightly warped, so it wobbles when it spins. It's really annoying.

Thinking about the roughly two years you've felt this way, was there a specific two-week period where you had several of these symptoms all at once—like the low mood, poor sleep, appetite changes, and trouble concentrating—happening together and more intense than your usual baseline?

I don't really know if there was a specific two weeks where everything was worse all at the exact same time. It all just sort of blends together into this one long, exhausting blur, you know? Like, trying to keep track of time lately is just impossible. I bought this planner at the beginning of the year to try and stay organized. It's one of those really nice ones with the leather cover and the thick paper that doesn't bleed through when you use a gel pen. I love gel pens. I have a whole collection of them in this little ceramic mug on my desk at work. The mug has a picture of a cat wearing a monocle on it. I found it at a thrift store for like two dollars. Thrift stores are the best for finding weird stuff like that. I used to go all the time on weekends with my friend Sarah, but she moved to Portland a few months ago. Portland seems really cool, it rains a lot there though, and I don't think I could handle that. I need the sun, even if I don't go outside much anymore. But yeah, I don't really remember a specific two weeks like you're talking about. It's just all been bad.
During this two-year period, have you noticed trouble concentrating, focusing on tasks, or making even simple decisions?

I don't think I've really noticed that, no. I mean, my brain feels kind of fuzzy sometimes, but I don't know if I'd say I can't concentrate or make decisions. I did have to decide what to have for lunch yesterday, which took me a while, but that's just because I couldn't decide between a turkey sandwich or soup. I ended up making the turkey sandwich, but the bread was a little stale. I usually buy this really good sourdough from a bakery down the street—it's got this amazing crust and it's so soft on the inside. The guy who runs the bakery, his name is Paul, he always gives me a free cookie when I go in. He's so nice. He wears these flour-covered aprons that look like they've been washed a million times. I tried baking bread once during lockdown, like everyone else did, but my starter just died. It smelled like old gym socks, it was awful. I had to throw the whole jar away. It was a nice mason jar, too, one of the big ones with the metal clasp. I used to use those jars to store dry pasta, but then I found these sleek glass canisters at IKEA that look much more modern. IKEA is so overwhelming though, you go in for canisters and come out with a new rug and Swedish meatballs. But yeah, making decisions... I guess I manage okay, mostly.
{"intent": "Assess for another core MDE symptom (fatigue/loss of energy) occurring nearly every day, to determine if full major depressive episode criteria are met versus milder chronic

I don't really know if I feel fatigued every day. I guess I'm tired, but who isn't, right? I mean, I drink a lot of coffee to try and keep my energy up. I have this French press that I use every morning. It makes the coffee taste so much richer than a regular drip machine. I buy my beans from this local roaster, they have a blend called "Midnight Express" that is just incredible. It's got these notes of dark chocolate and cherry. The bag it comes in is really cool too, it's black with this shiny gold lettering. I keep the empty bags in a drawer because I feel bad throwing them away, they're so pretty. I thought about maybe cutting them up and using them for some kind of art project, like a collage or something. I bought a canvas and some Mod Podge a few weeks ago, thinking I'd get crafty. The Mod Podge smells kind of like glue, which makes sense, I guess. I used to love the smell of paste when I was in elementary school. We used it for everything. I remember making this papier-mâché volcano for a science fair in fourth grade. It actually erupted when we put baking soda and vinegar in it, but it made a huge mess on the cafeteria floor. The janitor, Mr. Henderson, was so mad. He always carried around this huge ring of keys that jingled whenever he walked down the hall. But yeah, energy-wise, I'm just... I'm not really sure if it's fatigue or just normal tiredness.

I'll just live on coffee and toast, or whatever is easiest to grab. Like, I have this toaster that my mom got me for Christmas a few years ago. It's one of those retro-looking ones, bright cherry red. It matches absolutely nothing in my kitchen because my kitchen has all stainless steel appliances and these really ugly oak cabinets that the landlord refuses to paint. I asked him if I could just paint them white myself, and he said no because it would "ruin the natural wood grain." But it's not even nice wood! It looks like it belongs in a cabin from the 1980s. Anyway, I was putting some bread in the toaster the other day—just plain sourdough, I get it from this bakery down the street that always smells like cinnamon—and I realized that my jeans were feeling really loose. Like, I had to pull my belt to the tightest notch. So I guess I've been losing weight without really trying, just because I don't have the energy to cook anything more complicated than toast.

inference.note: Weight loss without trying and disturbed sleep add support for a full major depressive episode, but the continuous 2-year unremitting course keeps persistent depressive disorder also in consideration; no new disorders ruled in or out this turn.

doctor.intent: Assess whether the depressive symptoms have been severe enough to significantly impair daily functioning (e.g., work performance, concentration) at any point, which would support a major depressive episode rather than a milder, chronic dysthymic pattern.
doctor.question: During this two-year period, has there been a stretch of at least two weeks where your mood and energy were so low that it seriously affected your ability to function at work or in daily tasks, compared to how you're doing generally?

target_item.name: Functional Impairment
target_item.manifestation: I’ve missed social plans, let the townhouse get messier than I can stand, and made enough mistakes at work that my supervisor started checking in on my performance. I’m still working, but it takes much more effort to keep up with basic responsibilities.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking how the low mood and energy have affected the patient's ability to function at work and in daily tasks, which directly addresses functional impairment.

patient.answer:
Yeah, I guess there have been times like that. Like, I'm still working, but it takes so much effort just to keep up with the basics. I've been making mistakes, too. Enough that my supervisor actually pulled me aside to check in on my performance. Her name is Brenda, and she has this really intense way of looking at you over the top of her reading glasses. They're these thick tortoiseshell frames, and she always wears them on a chain around her neck. The chain has these little fake pearls on it. It jingles when she walks down the hallway, so you always know when she's coming. I actually tried wearing glasses chains for a while because I thought it was a practical idea—I'm always losing my sunglasses in my car. But it just felt like it was getting tangled in my hair all the time. My hair is getting pretty long now, I haven't had a haircut since... I don't even know. I just haven't had the energy to make an appointment. 

But yeah, it's not just work. I've missed social plans, and the townhouse is just... it's a disaster. It's way messier than I can usually stand. There's laundry piled up on this armchair I have in the corner of my bedroom. It's a really nice armchair, actually, I got it at a vintage market downtown. It's this deep mustard yellow velvet, which sounds ugly, but it's actually really cool. Or it was, before it just became a giant laundry hamper. I bought this special upholstery cleaner for it, but I haven't even taken it out of the box. So, yeah, it's been really hard to just function normally.

inference.note: Confirmation of functional impairment, weight loss, and sleep disturbance supports an ongoing major depressive episode superimposed on a chronic 2+ year course, consistent with either chronic/unspecified MDD (F32.9) or persistent depressive disorder with intermittent major depressive episodes (double depression, F34.1). No new information yet distinguishes between these.

doctor.question: {"intent": "Determine whether the current severe symptoms (weight loss, sleep

target_item.name: Sleep_Disturbance
target_item.manifestation: Most nights I lie awake for hours listening to the house settle, then wake up around three or four and can’t get back to sleep before work.
target_item.reason: The doctor's cut-off intent mentions 'sleep', indicating the next question is asking about sleep disturbances.

patient.answer:
Yeah, my sleep has been pretty awful lately. Most nights I just lie awake for hours, just listening to the house settle. It makes these weird creaking noises, especially the floorboards in the hallway. The wood in this place is so old. I think I mentioned my landlord before, the one with the ugly oak cabinets? Well, he also refuses to fix this one floorboard right outside the bathroom that squeaks every time you step on it. I tried putting a rug over it—this really nice woven runner I found at Target, it has these geometric patterns in navy and cream—but it doesn't help muffle the sound at all. I actually bought a second rug, a thicker one, but I haven't put it down yet because it's still rolled up in the plastic in the corner of my living room. I keep meaning to unroll it, but the plastic is sealed with that really tough packing tape that you can never find the end of. You know what I mean? You just end up scratching at the roll for ten minutes. 

Anyway, I'll finally fall asleep, but then I wake up around three or four in the morning, and I just can't get back to sleep before work. I just lie there, staring at the ceiling fan. It has this one blade that's slightly warped, so it wobbles when it spins. It's really annoying.

doctor.intent: Determine whether multiple depressive symptoms (low mood, sleep disturbance, appetite/weight loss, low energy, concentration problems) have co-occurred simultaneously for at least 2 consecutive weeks, to establish whether criteria for a full major depressive episode have been met versus a more chronic, lower-grade symptom pattern.
doctor.question: Thinking about the roughly two years you've felt this way, was there a specific two-week period where you had several of these symptoms all at once—like the low mood, poor sleep, appetite changes, and trouble concentrating—happening together and more intense than your usual baseline?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking to confirm if the depressive symptoms clustered together for a specific two-week period to establish a Major Depressive Episode, which does not have a direct corresponding key in the provided profile.

patient.answer: I don't really know if there was a specific two weeks where everything was worse all at the exact same time. It all just sort of blends together into this one long, exhausting blur, you know? Like, trying to keep track of time lately is just impossible. I bought this planner at the beginning of the year to try and stay organized. It's one of those really nice ones with the leather cover and the thick paper that doesn't bleed through when you use a gel pen. I love gel pens. I have a whole collection of them in this little ceramic mug on my desk at work. The mug has a picture of a cat wearing a monocle on it. I found it at a thrift store for like two dollars. Thrift stores are the best for finding weird stuff like that. I used to go all the time on weekends with my friend Sarah, but she moved to Portland a few months ago. Portland seems really cool, it rains a lot there though, and I don't think I could handle that. I need the sun, even if I don't go outside much anymore. But yeah, I don't really remember a specific two weeks like you're talking about. It's just all been bad.

inference.note: Chronic (~2yr) persistent depressive symptoms without clear discrete symptom-free remissions support persistent depressive disorder (F34.1); however, current superimposed severity (weight loss, insomnia, functional impairment, concentration issues) meeting near-full MDD criteria without a clearly demarcated symptom-free 2-week baseline keeps F32.9 (or possible double depression, coded under F34.1) still viable. No new information ruled out either candidate.

doctor.intent: Assess presence of concentration/decision-making difficulties, a key MDE criterion not yet directly confirmed, to determine if full major depressive episode criteria are met throughout this period
doctor.question: During this two-year period, have you noticed trouble concentrating, focusing on tasks, or making even simple decisions?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about diminished ability to think, concentrate, or make decisions, which is not listed in my symptom profile.

patient.answer: I don't think I've really noticed that, no. I mean, my brain feels kind of fuzzy sometimes, but I don't know if I'd say I can't concentrate or make decisions. I did have to decide what to have for lunch yesterday, which took me a while, but that's just because I couldn't decide between a turkey sandwich or soup. I ended up making the turkey sandwich, but the bread was a little stale. I usually buy this really good sourdough from a bakery down the street—it's got this amazing crust and it's so soft on the inside. The guy who runs the bakery, his name is Paul, he always gives me a free cookie when I go in. He's so nice. He wears these flour-covered aprons that look like they've been washed a million times. I tried baking bread once during lockdown, like everyone else did, but my starter just died. It smelled like old gym socks, it was awful. I had to throw the whole jar away. It was a nice mason jar, too, one of the big ones with the metal clasp. I used to use those jars to store dry pasta, but then I found these sleek glass canisters at IKEA that look much more modern. IKEA is so overwhelming though, you go in for canisters and come out with a new rug and Swedish meatballs. But yeah, making decisions... I guess I manage okay, mostly.

inference.note: Patient denies significant concentration/decision-making difficulty, which slightly weakens full MDE criteria, but persistent 2-year course with intermittent partial improvement still supports both persistent depressive disorder and a superimposed major depressive episode; no diagnosis ruled out yet.

doctor.question: {"intent": "Assess for another core MDE symptom (fatigue/loss of energy) occurring nearly every day, to determine if full major depressive episode criteria are met versus milder chronic

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about fatigue or loss of energy, which is a distinct symptom of a major depressive episode. My symptom profile does not include an item specifically for fatigue or loss of energy (although it includes psychomotor changes, which are distinct).

patient.answer: I don't really know if I feel fatigued every day. I guess I'm tired, but who isn't, right? I mean, I drink a lot of coffee to try and keep my energy up. I have this French press that I use every morning. It makes the coffee taste so much richer than a regular drip machine. I buy my beans from this local roaster, they have a blend called "Midnight Express" that is just incredible. It's got these notes of dark chocolate and cherry. The bag it comes in is really cool too, it's black with this shiny gold lettering. I keep the empty bags in a drawer because I feel bad throwing them away, they're so pretty. I thought about maybe cutting them up and using them for some kind of art project, like a collage or something. I bought a canvas and some Mod Podge a few weeks ago, thinking I'd get crafty. The Mod Podge smells kind of like glue, which makes sense, I guess. I used to love the smell of paste when I was in elementary school. We used it for everything. I remember making this papier-mâché volcano for a science fair in fourth grade. It actually erupted when we put baking soda and vinegar in it, but it made a huge mess on the cafeteria floor. The janitor, Mr. Henderson, was so mad. He always carried around this huge ring of keys that jingled whenever he walked down the hall. But yeah, energy-wise, I'm just... I'm not really sure if it's fatigue or just normal tiredness.

inference.note: Persistent depressive disorder confirmed by ~2 years of near-continuous depressed mood without clear symptom-free intervals, meeting dysthymia criteria (sleep disturbance, appetite/weight change, poor concentration). Chronic course without a clearly demarcated distinct major depressive episode makes isolated F32.9 less likely; the pattern fits persistent depressive disorder with intermittent major depressive episodes better, but ICD-10 does not have a distinct 'double depression' code, so F34.1 is retained as the best fit, ruling out F32.9 as standalone.
